title: The Cipher of Marseille's old port
premise: Ansel Delacroix, a deniable fixer for a diplomatic entity that exists only in sealed files, is approached by a woman named Yara who claims he saved her life years ago—a debt he has no memory of. As he investigates the favor he never performed, he uncovers a plot to destroy the Vieux-Port during an EU maritime summit, staged to resemble a gas main catastrophe, orchestrated by the same network that erased his own past. The trail leads to his late mentor's hidden ledger, an inheritance of secrets that names the conspirators and reveals Ansel himself was once their asset. In the end, Ansel exposes the attack without ever existing on any official record, chooses justice over reinstatement, and gives Yara the truth: the memory was hers, implanted to test whether conscience could be manufactured—and it could.
about_author: Coral Reyes spent a decade working port-side jobs along the Mediterranean before turning to fiction, drawing thrillers from the half-heard conversations of harbors at night. She lives between Marseille and Lisbon and writes under a pen name because, as she says, some stories are safer told by no one.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Was
chapters.summary: Ansel Delacroix receives a package containing a photograph of himself at a fire he has no memory of, plus a note: 'One life owed. Interest due.' POV Ansel. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: Embassy of Smoke
chapters.summary: Ansel queries his handlers about the date in the photo; they deny any operation existed. He visits the burned building site in Marseille. POV Ansel. Beat: first crack in his trust in the machinery that owns him.

chapters.title: Yara
chapters.summary: The stranger, Yara Kessab, explains she survived that fire because someone pulled her out—she has spent years finding him. Her certainty unsettles him more than threats would. POV Yara. Beat: warmth colliding with Ansel's suspicion.

chapters.title: Ledger of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Ansel traces the fire to his late mentor, Étienne Roux, and finds a hidden compartment in Roux's old apartment: a coded ledger. POV Ansel. Beat: grief rekindled into purpose.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Yara is nearly run down by a delivery van; Ansel realizes whoever erased the fire knows she found him. POV alternating. Beat: the debt becomes a shared target on their backs.

chapters.title: The Summit Calendar
chapters.summary: Decoding part of the ledger, Ansel finds references to 'Vieux-Port' and a date matching the EU maritime summit. POV Ansel. Beat: dread—the accident hasn't happened yet.

chapters.title: Gaslight
chapters.summary: City records show a gas main inspection scheduled under the port weeks before the summit—an inspection signed off by a dead engineer. POV inspector Camille Ferrand. Beat: institutional rot made personal.

chapters.title: What Roux Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: fifteen years earlier, Roux recruits a young, nameless operative—Ansel—for off-book work. POV Roux. Beat: tenderness shadowed by exploitation.

chapters.title: The Network Without a Name
chapters.summary: Ansel identifies a private security consortium, Meridian, whose contracts vanish from every database. He breaks into their Marseille office. POV Ansel. Beat: exhilaration curdling into violation—he finds his own file.

chapters.title: Asset 7
chapters.summary: His file shows he was Meridian property before Roux stole him out; the fire was Meridian destroying evidence, and Roux died for it. POV Ansel. Beat: identity collapse.

chapters.title: Yara's Memory
chapters.summary: Yara admits gaps in her own recollection of the rescue; therapy records suggest manipulation. They confront what they can trust in each other. POV Yara. Beat: intimacy forged in doubt.

chapters.title: Camille's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Inspector Ferrand finds the falsified inspection trail but is ordered to stand down by superiors tied to Meridian. POV Camille. Beat: the cost of integrity.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: The ledger decodes fully: the attack is set for the summit's opening night, disguised as infrastructure failure. Ansel has seventy-two hours and no official existence. POV Ansel. Beat: cold resolve.

chapters.title: Old Friends, New Prices
chapters.summary: Ansel calls in favors from smugglers and dockworkers of the Vieux-Port; one betrays him to Meridian for amnesty. POV dock boss Nabil. Beat: loyalty priced and sold.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Captured by Meridian, Ansel is offered reinstatement if he forgets everything again. He escapes using a trick Roux taught him. POV Ansel. Beat: choosing self over safety.

chapters.title: The Engineer's Daughter
chapters.summary: The dead engineer's daughter holds her father's real inspection report proving sabotage prep. Meridian closes in on her too. POV daughter Léa. Beat: inheritance as burden and weapon.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Ansel, Yara, Camille, and Léa pool their fragments: the plan targets the summit ferry terminal via the gas grid. POV rotating. Beat: strangers becoming a conspiracy of the decent.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: They map the port tunnels while Meridian sweeps for them; Ansel sends the evidence to forty journalists as insurance. POV Ansel. Beat: calm before the storm, love admitted quietly.

chapters.title: The Accident That Didn't Happen
chapters.summary: Summit night: they trigger a controlled shutdown of the gas grid minutes before detonation, forcing Meridian's team to abort or be caught. POV multiple. Beat: terror, precision, sacrifice—Nabil redeems himself and is wounded.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: The evidence detonates publicly instead: headlines, resignations, arrests—but Meridian's principals slip toward extradition-proof exits. POV Camille. Beat: victory with a bitter aftertaste.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ansel corners the last principal aboard a departing freighter and forces a confession onto record rather than killing him—justice that will survive him. POV Ansel. Beat: mastery of his own violence.

chapters.title: The Cipher Solved
chapters.summary: Roux's final cipher decodes to a message for Ansel: 'You were never theirs.' Ansel burns his file, gives Yara the truth of her implanted memory, and walks the sunlit Vieux-Port as simply a man. POV Ansel. Beat: peace earned, invisibility chosen at last.
